answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks using memory-hard state attestation. Agents log operational proofs across an execution trellis, imprinting each update with a verifiable pigment derived from sequential memory access. This forces an attacker onto a steep capital ledge, requiring dedicated RAM bandwidth and energy per forged identity. However, this imposes latency on resource-constrained edge agents and cannot stop adversaries with custom memory hardware.
